replies.name: gokayburuc
replies.text: @yvg AI always selects samples at the peak of the normal distribution curve.If your sample is either at the forward or backward point in the distribution, it will not present this as the optimum solution. In other words, artificial intelligence can sometimes overlook very good examples, and sometimes it can offer overly complex solutions for very simple ones.At this point, programmers who are familiar with the systems and know what each code does have a bigger role to play.

replies.name: Márton Salomváry
replies.text:
@yvg Speaking of merge conflicts, that's an important side-effect of PRs you might want to mention in your post. The longer a merge is delayed, the more and bigger the merge conflicts will be.

And, partially as a result of the above, collaborators will end up creating bigger PRs, that should have been small, separate, individually shipped changes.

replies.name: Yves Van Goethem :firefox:
replies.text: @mrc Super interested in the reactions :D Would be happy to get an anonymized summary of your exchanges when you feel like you're concluding the topic :)

replies.name: Márton Salomváry
replies.text:
@yvg Perfect timing, need exactly this on a project I recently joined. 

They practice the classic PR review ceremony. I the past few weeks since I've been collaborating, it has prevented zero bugs and facilitated zero meaningful conversations.

Meanwhile it delayed delivery by a day on the average and created 5-10% time overhead by creating merge conflicts.

Great write-up, thanks! Will drop this bomb on this team soon :D Long live Trunk Based Development!
